- **`dedupeSorted`:** es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`, so I used `uniq`. For sorted input it gives the same result: it keeps the first occurrence of each value, which is exactly what removing adjacent duplicates does. Your input range says the arrays are always sorted. If unsorted input ever mattered, `uniq` would differ, because it removes all duplicates and not only adjacent ones.
